title: DVBench: Benchmarking MLLMs for Understanding Dynamic Charts and Narratives in Data Videos
abstract: arXiv:2608.29711v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: While MLLMs have made significant strides in chart comprehension and video understanding, current evaluations largely isolate these capabilities, leaving a critical gap in understanding temporally evolving structured visual information. To address this gap, we introduce DVBench, a benchmark for evaluating MLLMs on data videos, a storytelling medium that integrates dynamic charts with structured narratives. We decompose data video understanding into five dimensions. DVBench comprises 300 real-world data videos and 1,000 human-verified QA pairs curated through a rigorous semi-automated pipeline. Extensive evaluations of nine MLLMs show that Gemini-3.1-Pro achieves the best overall performance, while Kimi-k2.5 is the strongest open-source model. We further identify two notable phenomena: open-source model performance does not scale strictly with parameter size, and narrative proficiency does not guarantee visual capability. Fine-grained ana

translated_title: DVBench：用于评估多模态大语言模型理解数据视频中动态图表与叙事能力的基准测试
translated_abstract: 尽管多模态大语言模型（MLLM）在图表理解和视频理解方面取得了显著进展，但当前的评估大多将这两种能力割裂开来，在理解随时间演化的结构化视觉信息方面留下了关键空白。为填补这一空白，我们提出了DVBench，一个用于评估多模态大语言模型在数据视频上表现的基准。数据视频是一种将动态图表与结构化叙事相结合的叙事媒介。我们将数据视频理解分解为五个维度。DVBench包含300个真实世界的数据视频和1000个经人工验证的问答对，这些问答对通过严格的半自动化流程整理而成。对九个多模态大语言模型的大量评估表明，Gemini-3.1-Pro取得了最佳整体性能，而Kimi-k2.5是最强的开源模型。我们进一步发现了两个值得注意的现象：开源模型的性能并不严格随参数规模的增大而提升，且叙事能力并不能保证视觉能力。
tldr: 提出DVBench基准，通过300个真实数据视频和1000个人工验证的问答对，从五个维度评估多模态大语言模型对数据视频中动态图表与叙事的理解能力，发现Gemini-3.1-Pro表现最佳，并揭示开源模型性能与参数规模、叙事能力与视觉能力之间并无必然的正相关关系。
en_tdlr: We introduce DVBench, a benchmark comprising 300 real-world data videos and 1,000 human-verified QA pairs across five dimensions to evaluate MLLMs' understanding of dynamic charts and narratives in data videos, showing that Gemini-3.1-Pro achieves the best performance and revealing that open-source model performance does not strictly scale with parameter size, and narrative proficiency does not guarantee visual capability.
